newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks end lower, just holding above 2,000.
newsitem.headline: French stocks end lower, just holding above 2,000.

text.p: French shares finished easier but clung stubbornly above the psychologically important 2,000 level on the CAC-40 index.

Despite London surging to new highs and Wall Street advancing, traders said Paris was mired in gloom over franc fragility, poor corporate earnings outlook and low expectations for the 1997 budget and tax reforms.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 15.09 points or 0.75 percent at 2,002.90 while the CAC-40 futures contract was down at 2,001 from 2,020.5 on Tuesday's close.

* President Jacques Chirac sought to inject some optimism into ministers who gathered for the first cabinet meeting since the summer break, while Prime Minister Alain Juppe said the government would move into top gear to tackle high unemployment
* CGT union leader Louis Viannet attacked the 1997 budget but stopped short of calling for a strike or joining a protest march called by the Force Ouvriere union for September 21
* Rhone-Poulenc ends unchanged at 134.50 francs, after regaining from earlier weakness. Broker Leven upgraded the stock to a "speculative buy" from "neutral"
* Scor continues firm, up six francs at 208.
* Scor was seen as a possible bid target following Swiss Re's acquisition of Prudential's M&G unit
Leven upgraded the re-insurance specialist to "buy" from "neutral" and set a target of 260 francs per share, while Du Bouzet sees the share hitting 250
* Cap Gemini finished 6.50 francs up at 222, or 3.02 percent, supported by positive sentiment following its 21 percent increase in first-half sales, higher than expected
* Another computer systems house, Axime, firmed 14 francs to 576 or 2.49 percent, benefiting from a rebound after recent sharp falls.
* Food group Danone lost six francs to 714, with total volume of 498,681 shares swollen by a block trade of 425,000 shares at 715 francs per share
* Credit Foncier was suspended pending the 70 francs per share offer by state bank CDC. The stock closed at 68.95 francs on Tuesday
* Alcatel Alsthom was up three francs at 398, or 0.76 percent, while Lagardere was down 2.74 percent at 124.30 francs. The rival bidders for Thomson SA could make firm offers by the end of September.
